what_its_for: Duloxetine is used to treat depression, anxiety, nerve pain (such as pain from diabetes), fibromyalgia (widespread muscle pain), and long-term musculoskeletal pain (like back pain or osteoarthritis pain). It works by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain called serotonin and norepinephrine.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with water. You may take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do NOT crush, chew, or open the capsule and sprinkle it on food unless your doctor specifically prescribes the sprinkle capsule form (Drizalma Sprinkle). If you use the sprinkle form, your doctor or pharmacist will give you separate instructions. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. Most adults start at 30 mg once a day and may increase to 60 mg once a day. Some conditions may require doses up to 120 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly — do not change your dose on your own. Do not stop taking duloxetine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms like dizziness, nausea, headache, or irritability.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day or close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store duloxetine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking duloxetine — it can increase the risk of liver problems and make side effects like dizziness or drowsiness worse. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Avoid taking other antidepressants, especially MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine, selegiline, or linezolid), within 14 days of starting or stopping duloxetine, as this can cause a serious and potentially life-threatening reaction. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, including blood thinners like aspirin or warfarin, as duloxetine can increase bleeding risk.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you experience: thoughts of hurting yourself or suicide (especially in children, teens, and young adults — risk may be higher at the start of treatment), unusual changes in mood or behavior, agitation, or feeling aggressive. Also contact your doctor if you have: severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); unusual bruising or bleeding; difficulty urinating; severe dizziness or fainting; fast or irregular heartbeat; seizures; a sudden severe headache; or high fever with stiff muscles and confusion (signs of a rare but serious condition called serotonin syndrome).
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in sleep, energy, or appetite within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, it may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer to feel the full benefit for depression, anxiety, or pain. Be patient and keep taking your medication as prescribed even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): May be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and falls — use extra caution. Children and teenagers: Not approved for use under age 7; use in children and teens requires close monitoring for mood changes and suicidal thoughts. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor — duloxetine may carry risks to the baby, especially if taken close to delivery. Breastfeeding: Small amounts may pass into breast milk; discuss risks and benefits with your doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Duloxetine may not be safe if you have significant kidney or liver disease — your doctor may adjust your dose or recommend a different medication.
